feature: M365 Health: build pillar scores live during an in-progress scan (part of epic #1045). GET /api/portal/assessment/status's radar.pillars used to come ONLY from a completed run that cleared the doc-generation coverage floor (portal-assessment.ts's `coverageRun`) -- during an active first scan `pillarCoverage` stayed [] for the run's entire duration, which is why /m365-health showed a static pre-scan empty state instead of scores building as checks land. Fix widens the source to `pillarSourceRun = coverageRun ?? (scanActive ? latestRun : null)`, reusing `getPillarCoverage` (pillar-coverage.ts) verbatim -- it already computes live off tenant_monitor_profiles rows that land the instant each check finishes, the same mechanism war-room-pillars already relies on. useM365HealthLive.ts now polls status/overview/metrics while useScanStatus().data.active is true (previously one-shot on mount), and HeroHealthScore.tsx/PillarGrid.tsx take a `scanRunning` prop that swaps the static pre-scan copy for 'building live' / journeyModel.ts's own SCANNING_PILLAR_CHIP wording.
notes: NOT YET RUN AGAINST THE DEPLOYED BUILD: this session's attempt to trigger the dev server pull+restart (trigger-deploy-and-wait.ps1, AGENT_PROTOCOLS.md section 4) was blocked by the harness's own permission classifier -- restarting the shared dev server mid-way through the heavy concurrent multi-session activity this environment had at the time was judged too disruptive to auto-approve. The fix landed on origin/main (bundled into commit e25de79a by a concurrent session's own commit -- verified byte-identical via `git diff e25de79a -- <each touched file>`, all empty), but the deployed dev server has not been confirmed to be running it yet, so D3/D4's new `data-testid` selectors (`pillar-grid` pre-existing, `m365-health-score-value` new) have not been exercised live. SHANE TO-DO: run `trigger-deploy-and-wait.ps1` (or redeploy however you normally do), then run this manifest via shaneapp://runTest.

MID-SCAN-WITH-NO-PRIOR-COMPLETED-RUN COULD NOT BE EXERCISED LIVE: verified via shaneapp://executeSql (2026-08-17) that the only two customers in this environment who have ever scanned (customer_id=1, the TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL testbed tenant, and customer_id=3) both already have a completed run clearing DOC_GATE_MIN_COVERAGE_PCT -- so `coverageRun` is non-null for both and `pillarSourceRun` resolves to it, not to the widened `latestRun` fallback this issue adds. There is no tenant in this environment on a genuine first-scan-with-nothing-completed-yet, so the NEW fallback branch itself is verified by code read (pillar-coverage.ts's getPillarCoverage is not completion-gated -- see the route's own comment) + a clean tsc --noEmit, not a live UI assertion -- documented honestly rather than faked, same class of gap as m365-health-breakdown-gate.json's #1099 locked-card note.

WHAT COULD BE VERIFIED LIVE: the testbed tenant (customer_id=1) genuinely has an ACTIVE run right now (msp_diagnostic_runs.status='running', confirmed via shaneapp://executeSql) alongside its real historical coverage-passing completed run -- a real, live case of `scan.active=true` AND `radar.pillars` non-empty at the same time. D1/D2 below assert exactly that combination, which exercises the regression this issue's fix must not introduce: HeroHealthScore/PillarGrid's real-score branch (`pillars.length > 0`) must keep winning over the new `scanRunning` copy branch, which only ever fires on the EMPTY-pillars path.

ENV VARS required in BuildConsole -> Settings -> Test Environment Variables: DEPLOY_URL, TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL / TEST_PORTAL_PASSWORD -- same testbed Assessment-role account m365-health-breakdown-gate.json / assessment-monitoring-rescan.json drive.

This manifest does not re-assert the Copilot Readiness Breakdown gate (#1099) or the copilotGate score fallback (#1108) -- see m365-health-breakdown-gate.json for those; this file is scoped to the pillar-grid/hero live-scan behaviour only.
